contains.zcull_on_demand_619: REWINDBOX_ZCULL_ON_DEMAND_619 (ios/IOSZcullOnDemand.h, ios/IOSRsxLabelAccess.h, RSXZCULL.cpp/.h, RSXThread.h, nv47_sync.hpp, nv406e.cpp, nv4097.cpp, rsx_methods.cpp, cellGcmSys.cpp, RPCS3IOSPerformance.cpp, title lever): Assassin's Creed (BLES00158, BLUS30089) only. Upstream marks a report location 'accessed' for the rest of the boot after the first access to a page that still holds a pending report; every report is then critical and every label write with a pipe flush, WAIT_FOR_IDLE or NOTIFY waits for the GPU in ZCULL_control::sync(). Build 617 logs (PID 65755, session 1, windows 17-28): 2,203-2,911 such waits per 5 s window, 4.15-4.32 s in all, every other ZCULL read path at 0, 14-17 FPS. On iOS the host page is 16 KiB: the GCM labels (4 KiB), the notifies (1 KiB) and local reports 0-703 share one page (label area 0x40300000 in the Black Ops II logs), so the RSX thread's own label read in write_gcm_label is enough to trigger it (independent review). With the lever, report pages stay protected; the RSX thread reaches the GCM label/report area and locked report pages through the unprotected view (label writes and reads, semaphore acquire, notify, flip label, conditional render and forwarder reads); a PPU or SPU access to a page with a pending report asks the RSX thread (pipe_flush_interrupt) to write every claimed report as sync() does, waits for it, then unprotects the page; an RSX copy out of a locked page writes them first; the HLE timestamp reads go through the protected view. The guest reads the same values, the labels no longer wait. A request not picked up in 2 s, not completed in 5 s, guest waits above 400 ms per second, more than 1,000 services per second, any other faulting thread, a stopping emulator or Accurate RSX reservation access keep or return the boot to the upstream mode; sync() and update() reached inside a pass return at once. COREPROF ZCULLDEMAND619 counts faults by label/report/other offset, services, waits, timeouts, the trip reason and, for every title, which access switched a location to the upstream mode
contains.zclip_pinned_affine_619: REWINDBOX_ZCLIP_PINNED_AFFINE_619 (RSXVertexPrologue.glsl, GLSLTypes.h, GLSLCommon.cpp, VKVertexProgram.cpp, title lever): Black Ops II (BLES01717) only, on top of REWINDBOX_ZCLIP_WINDOW_Z_616. The fallback compressed only window Z in (1, far] and passed every other vertex through; the pinned draws of the #13227 capture keep depth clip on and clamp off (NV4097_SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL = 1), so a triangle with a vertex in front of the near plane (window Z above 1e19) mixed an unchanged vertex with compressed ones and Vulkan clipped its edges at about 1e-21 of their length (host test) instead of at the near plane: the part of the first-person arm crossing the near plane vanished (Build 617 report: no texture on the back of the arm). For a clip range wholly above 1 every vertex now takes the same affine map of [near, far] onto [0.99, 1], unclamped beyond far: the hardware clip point equals the RSX clip point (host test, 5 edges) and every vertex in (1, far] keeps its Core 616 value. The SPIR-V of every other shader is byte-identical (glslang); Black Ops II vertex Metal libraries are compiled again once

contains.gpu_timing_621: REWINDBOX_GPU_TIMING_621 (ios/IOSGpuTiming.h, VKGSRender.cpp/.h, VKGSRenderTypes.hpp, VKPresent.cpp, VKCommandStream.cpp, vkutils/device.cpp/.h, RSXThread.cpp, RPCS3IOSPerformance.cpp, system_config.h, RPCS3IOSExperimentalPolicy.*, RPCS3IOSBootDiagnostics.h, System.cpp): every title. The reference traces print gpu_execution_ms=-1. In MoltenVK 1.4.2 (db66022) the MTLCommandBuffer GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime are read nowhere and VK_EXT_metal_objects does not export command buffers; vkGetPerformanceStatisticsMVK is a CPU commit-to-completion interval; Vulkan timestamp queries are sampled on Apple GPUs at Metal stage boundaries (a one-byte blit pass per timestamp, deferred to the end of the encoder batch, waiting for the previous encoders) and resolved from an MTLCounterSampleBuffer after completion. Each VKGSRender primary chunk (512) records a TOP_OF_PIPE timestamp when its recording begins and a BOTTOM_OF_PIPE one before vkEndCommandBuffer; the results are read without the WAIT bit when the chunk's fence signalled (frame-end sweep, at most 64) or before the chunk is reused (after the renderer's own wait), attributed to the renderer session and to the RSX frame whose on_frame_end closes the submission's epoch; overlapping submissions are united (never counted twice); VK_EXT_calibrated_timestamps pairs measure the GPU tick rate against the host clock (MoltenVK reports timestampPeriod 1.0) and place the GPU start on the host clock (queue delay, domain violations). COREPROF GPUTIME621 per window (coverage, busy, overlap, pending, unavailable, late and stop drops, units, probe CPU cost, blit passes); COREPROF FRAMECAUSE_EVENT gains gpu_execution_ms (or -1 with gpu_status), the waits and cause= with certainty=; GPU Timing Probe setting (Automatic = on) to measure its cost
contains.freeze_episode_621: REWINDBOX_FREEZE_EPISODE_621 (RPCS3IOSFreezeEpisode.h, RPCS3IOSPerformance.cpp, RPCS3IOSFreezeDump.cpp/.h, RPCS3IOSProfilerHelpers.h): the 5 s window trigger (running, no frame for 3 s, one group above half a core, one dump per 30 s) becomes episodes evaluated every 500 ms on a running-time clock that stops while paused, loading, stopping or suspended (no sample for 2 s); a busy stall begins at 3 s, a quiet one (below half a core) at 6 s, a guest-fault freeze (frozen state) at once; one FREEZE_DUMP per episode with a waits summary (PPU calls, SPU calls, SPU group states) and its episode id, the frozen state dumped too, 10 s floor; FREEZE_EPISODE begin/update/end lines (paused, suspended and loading time, flips during the episode, busiest threads, the RSX semaphore watch); recovery needs 10 flips over 1 s of running time, a later stall is a new episode

contains.spirv_disk_cache_634: REWINDBOX_SPIRV_DISK_CACHE_634 (ios/IOSSpirvCache.h, RSX/rsx_cache.h, RSX/VK/VKProgramPipeline.cpp): Build 629 logs: glslang ran again at every boot for every shader of the title's cache (1072 sources and 5.49 s of CPU at the Black Ops II multiplayer boot, 412 and 1.88 s in Assassin's Creed, 319 and 1.42 s in the Black Ops II menu, 5 ms each on the worker threads of the warmup). contains.fast_jit_load_634: REWINDBOX_FAST_JIT_LOAD_634 (ios/IOSJitLoad.h, Utilities/JITLLVM.cpp, Utilities/JITIOS.cpp, PPUThread.cpp): Build 629 logs: with every object cached, the PPU part of a boot took 2.2 to 4.4 s on one thread (object load 583 to 1127 ms, finalize 647 to 1420 ms, read 334 to 836 ms) and the window of checked objects kept only 26 to 41 of 72 to 174 modules. Values stay exact; codegen identities PPU a987639e9f838d1c / SPU 477a3fa442d27917 unchanged (PPUThread.cpp aliased, test/rpcs3_core636_test.py)
behaviour.core638: Instrumentation only: five relaxed atomic increments at the texture cache's existing predictor signals (section write-back, write-back with the upstream speculation flag still set, speculative copy, copy recorded at fault time, misprediction) and one COREPROF READPREDICT638 line per window beside READBACK555. Values, readbacks, submissions and defaults unchanged.
behaviour.core641: Log text only: three existing notice lines get the COREPROF AUDIO641 part=queue|producer|remoteio prefix. No audio path, buffer, value or cadence change.
behaviour.core645: iOS cellAudio: a period whose wait for an unwritten port timed out is no longer advanced without output. Guest periods, MIX events, timeouts, buffer size, tempo and the refill controller unchanged; disable_sampling_skip keeps the upstream path.
behaviour.core651: iOS cellAudio: the wait for an unwritten port also ends when the output ring holds under two blocks (one RemoteIO callback) after the period is due; the period is then output as on a timeout. Guest periods follow real time instead of slowing with the waits; buffer, tempo and refill controller unchanged; disable_sampling_skip keeps the upstream path. One field appended to the AUDIO641 queue line.
behaviour.core652: iOS Vulkan: fewer cyclic depth barriers (each ends the render pass): read-only chains, now including draws with the depth test off and no stencil write, keep one barrier; writes and the zeta fall-out keep theirs (host model on the real code: no read-after-write or write-after-read without a barrier, identical for writing loops). The render pass census only counts. Two fields appended to TEXCACHE621, one COREPROF RPASS652 line per window.
behaviour.core655: Assassin's Creed with the patched MoltenVK: read transitions of non-attachments no longer end the render pass (IPA 653: 4-11 same-framebuffer restarts per frame after vk::change_image_layout); every other title, and every other transition, as Core 652
behaviour.core659: Assassin's Creed and Black Ops II: early command buffer submissions at points without an open render pass (IPA 657: GPU idle 23-32 % of the frame while the RSX records after each ZCULL wait; OPT561 early_submits=0); Dragon Ball Z and God of War III as Core 655; every other title as Core 655; the two ZCULL counter lines in every title
behaviour.core660: SPU: decrementer reads of JIT blocks use g_timebase_offs (the C++ read's offset); cache hits with only known symbols skip the IR build, any other hit takes the IR path (same code linked). RSX: texture lookups reuse an exact earlier result while nothing they read changed (verified at each key's first reuse and by sampling; off for the boot at any difference); for Assassin's Creed the command buffer of a ZCULL report the game will wait for is submitted at the next pass boundary; for Assassin's Creed and Black Ops II the queue-depth hint is limited to command buffers holding the oldest pending query, and sent at least every 256 checks. Report values, texture results and guest-visible timing rules unchanged; no device measurement yet.
behaviour.core664: Every title with Passive Lock Fairness: after a passive-lock waiter starved and leaves, new writer locks of the other threads wait up to 100 us more (at most 500 us per writer lock, as before) before parking the PPU threads; every writer lock still taken in full. Guest-visible memory order and results unchanged; host model only (storm of heavy PUTLLC: PPU progress 3-11 % of its free speed without the window, 49-57 % with it; moderate rates unchanged within 2 %, mean of ten pairs); no device measurement yet.
behaviour.core668: Exactly Core 664: PPU threads at the default USER_INTERACTIVE relative priority, SPU QoS of Core 627, PPU grace of Core 664; no orchestrator thread, sampling or clock read. No codegen input changed; no device measurement
behaviour.core901: Automatic: exactly Core 668 (Vulkan on MoltenVK). With experimental.metal_renderer Enabled on a Metal 4 device, the RSX renderer is MTLGSRender: the display buffer from guest memory only; games that draw on the GPU show no image yet
behaviour.core902: Automatic: exactly Core 668 (Vulkan on MoltenVK). With experimental.metal_renderer Enabled on a Metal 4 device, the RSX renderer is MTLGSRender: draws, clears and presentation run on Metal 4 with neutral textures (no texture cache yet), single-sampled, without occlusion queries
behaviour.core903: Automatic: exactly Core 668 (Vulkan on MoltenVK). With experimental.metal_renderer Enabled on a Metal 4 device, the RSX renderer is MTLGSRender with textures, render-to-texture and readback, exact occlusion queries, MSAA and native overlays
behaviour.core904: Automatic: Core 668 behaviour (Vulkan on MoltenVK), with the JIT arena placed above 64 GiB when the low window is full. With experimental.metal_renderer Enabled on a Metal 4 device: the Core 903 renderer plus the boot program precompile, the persistent pipeline archive and the M3 gap paths
behaviour.core905: As Core 904; with experimental.metal_renderer Enabled, the complete Metal 4 renderer (M1-M5 part 1 with VK iOS ZCULL parity)
behaviour.core906: As Core 905; a title whose override file holds a retired setting keeps its other user values and accepts new ones; the Metal renderer reports every 5 s
behaviour.core907: As Core 906; Assassin's Creed computes the RSX H registers in float16 and begins fully cleared passes with load-op CLEAR (both per-title settings, Automatic on for AC only)
behaviour.core908: As Core 907; the texture lookup memo keeps up to 16 textures per sampler slot (same hit checks); measurement lines only otherwise (writer lock phases, freeze dump of polling threads and lwconds)
behaviour.core909: As Core 908; in God of War III (scope Automatic) NV308A/NV0039 writes revalidate only the textures over their range instead of every texture; measurement lines otherwise (epoch sources, MLAA application, freeze labels)
behaviour.core910: As Core 909; in God of War III (PUT horizon Automatic) a PUT change read below the horizon defers its texture epoch to the horizon; the prehash worker computes fewer results nobody reads; counters otherwise
behaviour.core911: As Core 910; in Black Ops II (accurate reservations) SPU threads polling with no-op PUTLLC sleep in bounded waits; the prehash look-ahead follows the worker results actually used
behaviour.core912: As Core 911 with both captures off (the default): one relaxed load per data-changing accurate PUTLLC and one call of the diagnostic thread per 500 ms; the stall dump lists more
behaviour.core914: As Core 912; a capture never holds an event prepared under another capture
